title: Meditate on Our Common Mortality: The Law of Death Denial
coreMove: Use mortality to reprice vanity, delay, and petty conflict so finite time directs attention toward what deserves life.
sourcePressure: The final law says death denial inflates vanity, triviality, and fear, while mortality awareness clarifies proportion, gratitude, urgency, and real investment.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Making mortality morbid or inspirational instead of a practical test of proportion and seriousness.

exampleSpecs.domain: an oncology nurse arguing with a sibling over an inheritance detail
exampleSpecs.audience: a caregiver whose proximity to death exposes pettiness
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a family spends final weeks litigating furniture
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she looks at the visitation schedule and moves the inheritance fight out of the patient's room before it steals another afternoon
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a visitor schedule taped beside a quiet infusion chair

exampleSpecs.domain: a retired ship captain putting off apology letters to former crew
exampleSpecs.audience: an older leader seeing delay as death denial
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether pride outlives the people who need the truth
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he places the names of three crew members beside stamped envelopes and writes the hardest letter first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three stamped envelopes aligned on a navigation chart

exampleSpecs.domain: a startup team fighting for title changes during a cash crisis
